newsitem.title: UK: British water disconnections ebb to six-year low.
newsitem.headline: British water disconnections ebb to six-year low.

text.p: Disconnections of British water customers fell to their lowest level since 1990 in the first half of the current financial year, latest figures released by industry watchdog Ofwat show.
Household disconnections fell to 1,974 in the period from 2,511 a year ago, down 21 percent Ofwat said.
"Companies should continue to offer every assistance to customers who have difficulty paying their water bills," Ofwat head Ian Byatt said in a statement.
Ofwat said the number of disconnections started to fall in 1992-93 after the watchdog issued guidelines on debt and disconnection.
Ofwat said current rates of disconnection were lower than before the industry was privatised.
Disconnections by water companies have been a sensitive political issue since privatisation.
